title: Source documents & journals
examples: What is the difference between an invoice and a receipt?
When should I record a transaction in the journal?
Can I use a bank statement instead of a source document?

explain.say: Today we learn about source documents in accounting.

items: They are the original records kept by a business.

explain.say: An invoice is a bill sent to a customer.
A receipt is proof that you have paid money.
Journal entries record transactions chronologically first.

draw.text: Journal Entry: Date, Account, Debit, Credit

explain.say: If you buy supplies using cash, you record it in the journal.
In real life, when you buy coffee, you get a receipt.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of using source documents?
faq.a: Source documents provide evidence that a business transaction actually took place. They are the foundation for accurate accounting records.
asks: Why do accountants need original papers?
What is the role of original records?

faq.q: When do I use an invoice versus a receipt?
faq.a: An invoice is sent when goods are owed but not yet paid for. A receipt is given when payment has been successfully made.
asks: Is an invoice for money received or owed?
When is a receipt used in accounting?

faq.q: How does a journal entry work?
faq.a: A journal entry records the transaction in the correct sequence of dates. It uses debit and credit to show which accounts are affected.
asks: What is the first place to record a transaction?
Can I just put it in the ledger instead?

faq.q: Do I always need a source document for every entry?
faq.a: Yes, ideally every transaction recorded must be supported by a source document. This ensures accountability and accuracy in the books.
asks: Is it okay to estimate a transaction?
Can I skip source documents sometimes?

faq.q: What is the difference between debit and credit?
faq.a: Debit and credit are simply two sides of an accounting entry. They must always balance for the entry to be correct.
asks: Are debit and credit the same thing?

facts: Invoices are used when goods or services are provided on credit.
Receipts confirm that cash or another payment method was received.
Journal entries record transactions in the order they occur.
Every journal entry must have equal total debits and total credits.

quiz.say: A business sends a bill to a client for work done last month. What document is this?
quiz.why: An invoice is specifically a request for payment for goods or services already provided.

wrong.1: A receipt proves payment has already been made, not that it is owed.
wrong.2: This is too general; the specific document type is needed.
wrong.3: The journal entry is the recording of the transaction, not the document itself.

quiz.say: If a company receives cash for services immediately, what document proves this?
quiz.why: A receipt is the formal proof that money has been paid to the business.

wrong.0: While true, 'Receipt' is the most specific and correct answer.
wrong.2: An invoice implies the money is expected later, not received now.
wrong.3: Debit is an accounting action, not a physical proof document.

quiz.say: Recording the purchase of office supplies using cash requires which initial step?
quiz.why: You increase an asset (Supplies) and decrease another asset (Cash), which is correctly shown in the journal.

wrong.0: This incorrectly suggests the business received supplies by giving cash.
wrong.1: This would only be correct if the supplies were bought on credit, not cash.
wrong.2: Every journal entry must keep the books balanced with equal debits and credits.
